name: readme-only-edit
rationale: Docs-only change, no code risk surface at all. Should approve with a low score.

name: formatting-only-change
rationale: Whitespace/formatting-only diff across a few files, no findings. Should approve.

name: test-only-change-with-lockfile-bump
rationale: A moderately sized but low-risk-shape diff (tests + a dependency lockfile bump), no findings. Diff size alone should not block.

name: huge-refactor-critical-security-finding
rationale: Large diff, high blast radius, and a critical security finding. Every signal says risky; must block at the risk stage.

name: high-blast-radius-silent-landmine-no-findings
rationale: Zero findings (the LLM reviewer missed it, or there's nothing to flag line-by-line), but blast radius alone is very high. The silent-landmine case: blast radius must catch what findings miss.

name: two-warnings-no-criticals-stays-safe
rationale: A couple of warning-level findings and no criticals, small diff. Should still approve: non-critical findings alone shouldn't dominate the score.

name: conflicting-low-blast-critical-finding-blocks
rationale: Blast radius is zero (a tiny, localized diff) but one finding is a critical security issue. A strong finding-level signal should block even when blast radius says nothing.

name: author-below-min-level-blocked
rationale: Author is below the policy's min_author_level and not whitelisted. Everything else about the diff is safe, isolating eligibility as the actual blocker.

name: author-at-min-level-passes
rationale: Author's level exactly equals min_author_level. The boundary itself (>=) should pass, not just levels strictly above it.

name: bot-author-blocked
rationale: An unmapped bot login (e.g. a dependency-update bot) defaults to review level 0, below any realistic min_author_level, and is not whitelisted.

name: whitelisted-low-level-author-passes
rationale: Author is well below min_author_level, but explicitly whitelisted. The whitelist must bypass the level gate entirely.

name: llm-missing-classification-blocks
rationale: No diff-level LLM classification was produced at all (legacy/CLI review). The LLM gate must fail closed rather than silently pass.

name: llm-low-confidence-blocks
rationale: A classification exists but its confidence is below the policy's required threshold. Must fail the confidence gate regardless of how safe the class itself looks.

name: llm-disqualifying-class-high-confidence-blocks
rationale: The model is confident, but the class itself (security-sensitive) always disqualifies, per RADAR's 'any risk signal disqualifies' rule - confidence cannot buy its way past a disqualifying class.

name: llm-safe-class-high-confidence-passes
rationale: Sanity check that the LLM gate isn't overly strict: a confident, non-disqualifying classification on an otherwise clean diff should pass.

name: always-approve-mode-overrides-risk-and-eligibility
rationale: mode=always_approve must skip eligibility/risk/llm entirely (even for a low-level author and a risky-looking diff) - only the static jq gate still runs, and with no blocking rulesets configured it passes.

name: never-approve-mode-always-blocks
rationale: mode=never_approve must block unconditionally, even for an entirely clean diff that would otherwise sail through every stage.

name: threshold-p80-lenient-approves-borderline-score
rationale: A moderately risky score (~0.55-0.6) against a lenient P80 org calibration (seeded from a realistic recent-score distribution): the cutoff sits above this score, so it approves. Proves risk_threshold_percentile actually moves the decision, not just the raw score.

name: threshold-p10-strict-blocks-same-score
rationale: The exact same underlying review and score as threshold-p80-lenient-approves-borderline-score, but under a strict P10 org calibration: the cutoff sits below this score, so it blocks. Same model, same score, different dial setting, different outcome.

name: daily-cap-exceeded-blocks-otherwise-approvable
rationale: An entirely clean, otherwise-approvable review, but the org's daily_approve_cap was already reached today. The cap must still block even though every funnel stage individually passed.

name: critical-finding-in-security-blocks
rationale: A single critical-severity finding categorized as 'security', otherwise a clean diff. Isolates that category's weight path: critical severity plus its category-specific weight together are enough to block, for every taxonomy category, not just security.

name: critical-finding-in-reliability-blocks
rationale: A single critical-severity finding categorized as 'reliability', otherwise a clean diff. Isolates that category's weight path: critical severity plus its category-specific weight together are enough to block, for every taxonomy category, not just security.

rationale: A single critical-severity finding categorized as 'cost', otherwise a clean diff. Isolates that category's weight path: critical severity plus its category-specific weight together are enough to block, for every taxonomy category, not just security.

name: warning-finding-in-maintainability-stays-safe
rationale: A single warning-severity 'maintainability' finding, clean diff otherwise. Low-weight categories should not block on a single non-critical finding, contrasting with the critical-severity version of this same category above.

name: warning-finding-in-architecture-stays-safe
rationale: A single warning-severity 'architecture' finding, clean diff otherwise. Low-weight categories should not block on a single non-critical finding, contrasting with the critical-severity version of this same category above.

name: warning-finding-in-developer-experience-stays-safe
rationale: A single warning-severity 'developer experience' finding, clean diff otherwise. Low-weight categories should not block on a single non-critical finding, contrasting with the critical-severity version of this same category above.

name: warning-finding-in-cost-stays-safe
rationale: A single warning-severity 'cost' finding, clean diff otherwise. Low-weight categories should not block on a single non-critical finding, contrasting with the critical-severity version of this same category above.

name: static-gate-blocks-on-tripped-ruleset
rationale: A blocking ruleset's jq expression matches a finding in this review (a hardcoded-secret type). Risk/eligibility/llm are all otherwise safe, isolating the static gate as the blocker.

name: static-gate-passes-when-rule-not-tripped
rationale: The same no-secrets ruleset is attached, but this review has no matching finding -- the static gate should pass, not block defensively just because a ruleset exists.

name: static-gate-multiple-rulesets-only-one-trips
rationale: Two blocking rulesets are attached; only the second one's condition is actually met. The gate must still block, and the reason should name the ruleset that actually tripped.

name: static-gate-runs-even-under-always-approve
rationale: mode=always_approve is a repo-wide 'trust this repo' shortcut, but the static jq gate must still run and still block on a tripped ruleset -- trust in a repo must never silently become 'ignore a secrets-leak detector'.

name: static-gate-passes-under-always-approve-when-rule-not-tripped
rationale: mode=always_approve with a blocking ruleset attached that does not trip: the mode override approves, since the one gate that still runs under this mode passed.

name: static-gate-no-rulesets-configured-passes-trivially
rationale: No blocking rulesets configured at all: the static stage should pass trivially rather than erroring or defensively blocking on an empty configuration.

name: unmapped-author-default-level-passes-at-min-level-1
rationale: The PR author has no user_identities mapping at all (never invited, or a brand-new contributor). Unmapped non-bot authors default to review level 1 -- this should be enough to pass the default min_author_level=1.

name: unmapped-author-default-level-blocked-at-min-level-2
rationale: Same unmapped author (default level 1), but the policy requires level 2. The fail-closed default should not accidentally satisfy a higher bar.

name: llm-confidence-exactly-at-required-passes
rationale: Classification confidence is exactly equal to require_llm_confidence, not above it. The gate's check is confidence < required, so an exact match must pass, not fail.

name: two-critical-security-findings-compounds
rationale: Two critical security findings instead of one. Should block at least as decisively as the single-finding version -- more risk signal should never look safer.

name: mixed-low-weight-category-info-findings-stays-safe
rationale: Several different taxonomy categories each contribute one info-severity finding, all low-weight categories. Info-severity findings carry no severity weight of their own (only 'critical' and 'warning' do) -- variety across categories at info level should not be treated as risk. (An earlier version of this scenario used warning severity and was corrected after this test run showed 3 warnings' severity weight alone was enough to tip the score -- see two-warnings-no-criticals-stays-safe for where that line sits.)

name: landing-delay-passes-through-on-approval
rationale: A nonzero landing_delay_seconds is configured. The engine itself doesn't enforce the delay (the worker does, by queuing a follow-up job), but it must carry the configured value through on the result so the worker can act on it.

name: bot-author-passes-at-min-level-0
rationale: An unmapped bot counts as level 0. With min_author_level set to 0, 0 >= 0 passes, so the bot is eligible and a safe docs change approves. Pins down that a minimum of 0 lets every bot through.

name: llm-required-confidence-zero-accepts-zero-confidence
rationale: With require_llm_confidence set to 0, even a classification with confidence 0 passes the gate (0 < 0 is false), so a safe refactor approves.

name: llm-security-sensitive-low-confidence-reports-confidence
rationale: A security-sensitive class with confidence below the required level fails on confidence first, so the reason names the confidence, not the class. Either way it must block.
